title: Is the electric car market still growing?
question: Are electric car sales still growing worldwide, and where is the growth coming from?
notice: Example report. It shows what the skill produces. The figures follow public reports from mid-2025 (IEA Global EV Outlook 2025, BloombergNEF, ACEA), but this file was written by hand, not by a live run, so the header counts are illustrative. Check the sources before reusing a number.
tldr: Yes. More than 17 million electric cars were sold in 2024, over 1 in 5 new cars worldwide [1]. China made almost two thirds of those sales, while Europe stayed flat [2].

takeaways.text: Electric car sales passed 17 million in 2024. That is more than 1 in every 5 new cars sold.
China is the engine. It sold over 11 million electric cars, almost half of all new cars sold there.
Europe stalled at about 3.2 million, and the United States grew a little, to about 1.6 million.
Batteries got much cheaper. Pack prices fell about 20% in 2024, the biggest drop since 2017.
The IEA expects more than 20 million sales in 2025, about 1 in 4 new cars.

sections.heading: How fast are sales growing?
paragraphs: Electric car sales grew by about 25% in 2024, to more than 17 million [1]. That is slower than the huge jumps of 2021 and 2022, but the market is now much bigger, so each year adds millions of cars [3].
The IEA's outlook says sales should pass 20 million in 2025. That would make about 1 in 4 new cars electric [2]. Early 2025 sales were up about a third on the year before [2].

images.alt: An electric car plugged into a public charging station
images.caption: Public charging points are spreading fast, mostly in China.

sections.heading: Where is the growth coming from?
paragraphs: **China** sold more than 11 million electric cars in 2024. That is more than the whole world sold just two years before [2]. Almost half of all new cars sold in China were electric.
**Europe** stayed flat at about 3.2 million. Some subsidies ended, and EU rules on car emissions only tighten again in 2025 [2]. Counts for the EU alone show battery-only cars slipping a little [5].
**The United States** grew about 10%, to about 1.6 million. About 1 in 10 new cars sold there was electric [2].

sections.heading: Are electric cars getting cheaper?
paragraphs: Batteries are the most expensive part of an electric car. Their average price fell about 20% in 2024, to $115 per kWh [4]. Cheaper batteries make cheaper cars possible.
In China, most electric cars sold in 2024 already cost less than similar petrol cars [2]. In Europe and the United States, electric cars still cost more to buy on average [2].

claims.text: More than 17 million electric cars were sold worldwide in 2024.
Electric cars were more than 20% of new car sales in 2024.
China sold more than 11 million electric cars in 2024.
US electric car sales grew about 10%, to about 1.6 million.
Average battery pack prices fell about 20% in 2024, to $115 per kWh.
claims.note: Only BloombergNEF's yearly survey reports this exact figure.

claims.text: Most electric cars sold in China in 2024 cost less than similar petrol cars.
claims.note: Only the IEA report makes this price comparison.

claims.text: Electric car sales in Europe were flat in 2024.
claims.note: The IEA says sales held at about 3.2 million. ACEA says battery-only cars fell a little in the EU. They count different things (all of Europe and plug-in hybrids vs EU battery-only cars), so both can be true.

unconfirmed.note: The year was not over when this report was written. The 20 million figure is a forecast.

unconfirmed.text: How many people sell an electric car and go back to petrol.
unconfirmed.note: We found no large, recent survey on this.
